newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end slightly off as mining run slows.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end slightly off as mining run slows.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange made small overall losses Friday as investors took profits, particularly in the mining sector, after a recent run of gains.
The profit-taking was expected to ease up on Monday, leaving the market stable again, brokers said.

According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index fell 0.27 percent Friday to 2,263.41 points while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.47 percent to 3,267.97. Volume was an improved 46 million soles ($17.4 million) on 2,432 trades.

"It was a very quiet session with investors liquidating some positions in polymetallic miners because they have made enough since the rally began due to the rise in zinc prices," said Percy Romero of Fortuna brokerage.

He predicted that cement companies and breweries would do well in coming weeks on the effects of the gathering El Nio weather phenomenon. It has already brought an Indian summer to the coast and is expected to cause infrastructure damage from flooding in coming months.
In the mining sector, Milpo fell 2.30 percent to 46.40 soles Friday, while Morococha was off 1.96 percent to 9.99 soles, and Atacocha slipped 1.82 percent to 2.70 soles.
But Manuel Torres of Finvest, warned: "We cannot leave the polymetallic stocks aside because zinc prices are strong, around $1,470 per tonne, and are expected to reach $1,500 soon."
